---
title: "Example Files"
---

Small, complete examples of the file types you will work with in this
course. Every file is meant to be **opened, edited, and run in
Positron** — download it, break it, fix it, make it your own.

The two scripts and both notebook templates all analyze the same
course dataset with the same steps — read the data, normalize counts,
fit a linear model, make plots — so you can compare languages and
formats side by side.

## The dataset

RNA-seq gene-expression counts from the gut of 80 threespine
stickleback (*Gasterosteus aculeatus*): 2 host genotypes (A, B) x 2
microbiota treatments (conventional, mono-associated), 20 fish per
group, 600 genes. One tab-separated file, ~160 KB: a header line plus
one row per fish, with columns `Individual`, `Genotype`, `Microbiota`,
`Geno&Micro`, then `Gene1` … `Gene600` (raw read counts).

| Download | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| <a href="Data_Folder/Stickle_RNAseq.tsv" download>Stickle_RNAseq.tsv</a> | The course dataset used by all the example files below |

Save it anywhere, but the example scripts will find it automatically
if you keep the folder layout of the course repository
(`Data_Folder/` and `Examples_Folder/` side by side). If the scripts
don't find a local copy, they download it from this website.

## Shell scripts (Week 2)

Five small, heavily commented bash scripts from Lecture 02 — everyday
tools you can use on your own computer, and working examples of
arguments, pipes inside scripts, and scripts chained *by* pipes. After
downloading, make them executable once (that's the Lecture 02
permissions lesson in action):

``` bash
chmod +x *.sh
```

| Download | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| <a href="Examples_Folder/scripts_week02/file_inventory.sh" download>file_inventory.sh</a> | Writes a report of every file in a folder, grouped by file type and ordered by total size (largest first), with each file's permissions and size |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/scripts_week02/make_project.sh" download>make_project.sh</a> | Creates the recommended project directory structure from Lecture 01, with template `README.md`, `.R`, `.py`, and `.qmd` files |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/scripts_week02/filter_rows.sh" download>filter_rows.sh</a> | Pipeline part 1: filters rows of a tab-separated table (e.g. the course dataset) by the value of a named column |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/scripts_week02/total_counts.sh" download>total_counts.sh</a> | Pipeline part 2: totals the gene-count columns per fish; reads the output of `filter_rows.sh` — e.g. `./filter_rows.sh Genotype A < Stickle_RNAseq.tsv \| ./total_counts.sh` |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/scripts_week02/backup_project.sh" download>backup_project.sh</a> | Makes a dated `.tar.gz` snapshot of a project folder, skipping the regenerable `output/` folder |

## A first Python script (Week 3)

The Lecture 03 warm-up script: the same script mechanics as the Week 2
shell scripts above (shebang on line 1, `chmod +x` once, run with
`./`), but with Python inside. It reads the course dataset — one line,
because the file is tidy — totals the 600 gene columns per fish, and
saves a boxplot by genotype-x-microbiota group into `results/`.

| Download | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| <a href="Examples_Folder/scripts_week03/plot_stickleback.py" download>plot_stickleback.py</a> | Your first Python script: read `Stickle_RNAseq.tsv`, total the gene counts per fish, save a quick boxplot by group — a preview of L05-L07 |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/scripts_week03/plot_stickleback_walkthrough.ipynb" download>plot_stickleback_walkthrough.ipynb</a> | The same analysis as a Jupyter notebook that explains every step — run it cell by cell in Positron to see what each line does |

## Computational lab notebook templates

Templates for keeping a dated, honest record of an analysis —
objective, data provenance, methods, results, dead ends, next steps —
each with a fully worked example entry using the dataset above. Copy
the template, rename it (e.g. `2026-10-06_rnaseq-qc.qmd`), and fill it
in as you work.

| Download | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| <a href="Examples_Folder/lab_notebook_template.qmd" download>lab_notebook_template.qmd</a> | Quarto notebook template (R code chunks); render to a self-contained HTML |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/lab_notebook_template.ipynb" download>lab_notebook_template.ipynb</a> | Jupyter notebook template (Python), same structure |

## Python tutorial notebooks

A series of hands-on Jupyter notebooks for learning Python, created by
[Parisa Hosseinzadeh](https://knightcampus.uoregon.edu/parisa-hosseinzadeh)
(Knight Campus Department of Bioengineering) for her course on
data-driven design in engineering, offered in parallel with this one —
used here with thanks, and lightly adapted to run in Positron. Each
notebook opens with a small exercise, then walks you through the ideas
needed to solve it.

They pair with lectures
[L05](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_05_BioE_Comp_Tools_2026.qmd)-[L07](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_07_BioE_Comp_Tools_2026.qmd),
where we introduce Python scripting: work through s1-s6 alongside L05,
s7-s8 alongside L06-L07, and s9 when you want more linear algebra. To
run one, download it, open it in Positron, choose a Python interpreter
if prompted (top right), and run cells with `Shift + Enter`.

| Download | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| <a href="Examples_Folder/python_tutorials/s1_variables.ipynb" download>s1_variables.ipynb</a> | Getting started: `print`, assigning variables, types and type conversion, arithmetic and comparisons |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/python_tutorials/s2_ConditionalStatements.ipynb" download>s2_ConditionalStatements.ipynb</a> | `if` / `elif` / `else`, comparison and logical operators — guess the mystery number |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/python_tutorials/s3_Loops.ipynb" download>s3_Loops.ipynb</a> | `for` and `while` loops, `range`, changing flow with `continue` and `break` |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/python_tutorials/s4_Functions.ipynb" download>s4_Functions.ipynb</a> | Writing functions: arguments, docstrings, `return`, input checking, raising errors, importing packages |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/python_tutorials/s5_Lists.ipynb" download>s5_Lists.ipynb</a> | Lists, indexing and slicing; find min/max/median by hand, then the easy way; tuples and sets |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/python_tutorials/s6_Dictionaries.ipynb" download>s6_Dictionaries.ipynb</a> | Dictionaries: key-value storage, looping over items, saving to csv/json/text/pickle |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/python_tutorials/s7_PandasDataframe.ipynb" download>s7_PandasDataframe.ipynb</a> | Pandas data frames and data cleaning |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/python_tutorials/s8_PlottingData.ipynb" download>s8_PlottingData.ipynb</a> | Plotting with matplotlib and seaborn, on a real dataset of college majors |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/python_tutorials/s9_NumpyMatrices.ipynb" download>s9_NumpyMatrices.ipynb</a> | Numpy arrays and matrix operations: indexing, dot products, transpose, rank, determinant, inverse, eigenvalues |
| <a href="Examples_Folder/python_tutorials/W1L2_Overfitting.ipynb" download>W1L2_Overfitting.ipynb</a> | Bonus — model evaluation and overfitting: polynomial fits, AIC, and train/test splits |

## Example GitHub README

An example of the top-level `README.md` of a GitHub repository for a
genomics study: project overview, a data-availability table pointing
to the NCBI databases where the data were deposited (SRA/BioProject,
GEO, BioSample, and the reference genome assembly), repository
structure, environment, and reproduction steps. Look at it both ways:
rendered, and as plain-text source in Positron.

| Download | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| <a href="Examples_Folder/example_README.md" download>example_README.md</a> | Example repository README for a genomic-data analysis project (accession numbers are placeholders) |

## Before you run them

- **R packages:** install once with
  `install.packages(c("readr", "dplyr", "ggplot2"))`.
- **Python packages:** the course environment already has `pandas`,
  `numpy`, `matplotlib`, and `seaborn`; add the linear-model package
  once with `pip install statsmodels`.
- In Positron, run scripts line by line with `Cmd/Ctrl + Enter`,
  render `.qmd` files with `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + K`, and run notebook
  cells with `Shift + Enter`.
